chapters.title: Guarding the gospel and remembering mercy

parts.text: Paul urges Timothy to remain at Ephesus and stop teachers promoting different doctrine, fables, and endless genealogies. Instruction should produce love from a pure heart, good conscience, and sincere faith, not empty disputes. Some desire to teach the law without understanding it. The law is good when used rightly, confronting lawlessness and conduct contrary to the sound teaching of the gospel entrusted to Paul.

Paul thanks Christ for placing him in ministry despite his former blasphemy and persecution. He received abundant mercy, illustrating Christ’s patience toward sinners who would believe for everlasting life. Christ came to save sinners, and Paul calls himself foremost among them before praising the eternal God. He charges Timothy to fight faithfully in keeping with earlier prophecies, holding faith and a good conscience, unlike those who made shipwreck and required discipline.

Paul calls for prayers and thanksgiving for everyone, including rulers, so believers may live peacefully in godliness. Such prayer pleases God, who desires people to be saved and know the truth. There is one God and one mediator between God and humanity, Christ Jesus, who gave himself as a ransom for all. Paul identifies his appointed work as preaching this testimony and teaching the Gentiles in faith and truth.

Men should pray with holy hands, free from anger and doubting. Women should display modesty and good works rather than costly ornament. Paul instructs women to learn quietly in submission and says he does not permit a woman to teach or usurp authority over a man, grounding this in Adam’s formation and Eve’s deception. He closes with a statement about being saved in childbearing, conditioned on continuing in faith, love, holiness, and sobriety.

Paul describes oversight as a good work requiring blameless character, marital faithfulness as a husband of one wife, self-control, hospitality, and ability to teach. An overseer must avoid violence, greed, and drunkenness, manage his household well, have a good reputation outside the church, and not be a novice vulnerable to pride. Deacons likewise must be trustworthy, sober, tested, and faithful in conscience and household leadership. Their wives must be dignified, faithful, and free from slander.

Paul writes these instructions so Timothy will know proper conduct in God’s household if his visit is delayed. The church of the living God is the pillar and ground of truth. He concludes by declaring the great mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.

chapters.title: Faithful teaching and a godly example

parts.text: The Spirit warns that some will abandon faith for seducing spirits and doctrines of devils, including prohibitions on marriage and foods God created to be received thankfully. God’s creation is good and sanctified by his word and prayer. Timothy should remind believers of these truths, nourish himself in sound teaching, reject profane tales, and train in godliness. Unlike bodily exercise with limited benefit, godliness holds promise for both present and future life, grounding labor in hope in the living God.

Timothy must command and teach these things and answer possible contempt for his youth through exemplary speech, conduct, love, spirit, faith, and purity. Until Paul comes, he should devote himself to public reading, exhortation, and doctrine. He must not neglect the gift associated with prophecy and the elders’ laying on of hands. Wholehearted attention will make his progress evident. Paul urges him to persevere in his life and teaching, saying that in doing so he will save himself and those who hear him.

chapters.title: Care for widows and responsible oversight

parts.text: Timothy should treat older and younger believers as family, with respect and purity. Widows genuinely without support deserve the church’s care, but relatives must first provide for their own households. Paul gives qualifications for enrolling older widows, including age, faithfulness, and a record of good works. He warns about younger widows becoming idle or abandoning their commitment and counsels marriage and household responsibility. Family support allows church resources to reach those truly alone.

Elders who lead well, especially in teaching, deserve honor and support. Accusations require witnesses, while sin must be rebuked without favoritism. Timothy should avoid hasty laying on of hands or sharing responsibility for others’ sins and keep himself pure. Paul also advises a little wine for his recurring ailments. He reminds Timothy that some sins and good works are immediately visible, while others become evident later.

Servants should honor their masters so God’s name is not discredited, and serve believing masters especially well as beloved brethren. Paul warns against teachers who reject Christ’s wholesome words, cultivate disputes, and confuse material gain with godliness. True gain is godliness with contentment: people bring nothing into the world and take nothing out. The determination to become rich exposes people to destructive temptations, and love of money has led some from faith into sorrow.

Timothy must flee these dangers, pursue righteousness and love, and fight the good fight of faith, keeping his charge until Christ appears. Paul praises God’s unmatched sovereignty and immortality. Wealthy believers should trust God rather than riches, be generous, and become rich in good works with the future in view. Timothy must guard what has been entrusted to him and avoid empty talk and claims of knowledge that draw people from faith.
